title: Delete and limit Google Maps Timeline
keywords: GPS routes visits coordinates location history travel movements
summary: Review old routes and set a shorter retention period.
steps: Open Google Maps on the device that holds Timeline data. Tap your profile, then Your Timeline.
Open More → Location and privacy settings. Delete a date range or all Timeline data after reviewing what you want to keep.
Use Auto-delete Timeline or turn Timeline off to limit future retention. Review other Google activity controls separately.

title: Remove unnecessary Google Contacts
keywords: address book synced email phone people vcard
summary: Remove stored address-book entries you no longer need.
steps: Open Google Contacts and select the entries you want to remove.
Choose More → Delete → Move to trash.
Review Trash if you need immediate permanent removal. The change can sync to your devices.

title: Delete or auto-delete Google activity
keywords: search browse youtube watch web app myactivity clicks viewing retention
summary: Review past account activity and shorten its retention.
steps: Open your Google Account → Data & privacy → History settings.
Select the activity type you want to manage, such as YouTube History or Web & App Activity where available.
Use Manage activity to delete past entries. Set Auto-delete and confirm a retention period.

title: Review Google ad topics and personalization
keywords: inferred topics preferences profiling ads targeting personalized interests
summary: Reduce how saved profile and activity signals are used for ads.
steps: Open My Ad Center and select Manage Privacy.
Review your account information and activity used to personalize ads.
Turn off the activity inputs you want to exclude, or switch off personalized ads in My Ad Center.

title: Stop Instagram contact uploads
keywords: address book synced contacts phone contacts uploading people
summary: Stop future contact uploads and review contacts already uploaded.
steps: Open Instagram settings and find Accounts Center → Your information and permissions → Upload contacts.
Choose your Instagram account and turn off Connect contacts. Review this on every device with the account.
In Accounts Center on the web, look for Manage contacts and review the option to delete previously uploaded contacts.

title: Review Instagram followers and account visibility
keywords: following followers relationships social graph people circle network
summary: Reduce visibility of the account and review who follows it.
steps: Open Instagram settings and find Account privacy.
If the account supports it, enable Private account.
Review your followers and remove the accounts you no longer want to have access.

title: Review sensitive Instagram messages
keywords: DM chats inbox conversations message threads private communication
summary: Review conversations containing information you want to limit.
steps: Open your Instagram inbox and review conversations with sensitive information.
For a message you sent, use the message menu → Unsend if you want to remove it from the conversation.
Recipients may already have seen or saved the message.

title: Review Instagram logins and enable two-factor authentication
keywords: login ip devices sessions authentication password unknown sign ins
summary: Review devices and strengthen account sign-in.
steps: Open Accounts Center → Password and security → Where you're logged in.
Review the listed sessions and log out of any you do not recognize.
Under Password and security, open Two-factor authentication and follow the prompts.

title: Review Instagram ad preferences
keywords: inferred profile topics targeting ads personalization advertisers interests
summary: Check which topics and signals inform ads on your account.
steps: Open Accounts Center → Ad preferences and select your Instagram account if prompted.
Review the ad topics and available activity-based controls.
Apply the preferences you want. Available controls can vary by account and region.

title: Limit visibility of Spotify listening activity
keywords: streams songs artists plays listening watched music history friends feed listening patterns
summary: Reduce who can see what you listen to.
steps: In Spotify, open Settings and privacy → Privacy and social.
Turn off Listening activity and Recently played artists if you want to hide them from other listeners.
Use Private Session for temporary privacy. These sharing controls address visibility to others.

title: Review Spotify tailored-ad controls
keywords: targeting interests advertising profiling preferences personalized ads
steps: Open your Spotify account page and find Privacy Settings.
Review the available tailored-ad controls and turn off the processing options you do not want.
Review Spotify's privacy choices page for available account data requests.

title: Hide Spotify followers and following lists
keywords: followers following friends social graph connections profile
summary: Limit who can see your social connections in Spotify.
steps: In the mobile Spotify app, open Settings and privacy → Privacy and social.
Turn off Followers & following to hide these lists on your profile.

title: Review Spotify precise location access
keywords: country territory connection ip location geography geolocation permission
summary: Distinguish network location in the export from precise device location access.
steps: In Spotify mobile settings, open Privacy and social and check Precise location if the control is available.
Turn off precise location if you do not need the features it supports.
Review the Spotify export documentation for what the country and IP fields represent.

title: Review Spotify app access and account sessions
keywords: IP remote devices third party apps integrations unauthorized login connected accounts sessions
summary: Check whether other devices or services still have access.
steps: Open your Spotify account page → Manage apps and remove access from apps you do not use.
If you suspect unauthorized access, change your password and use Sign out everywhere under Security and privacy.
Remove partner devices from Manage apps where needed.
